name: MonarchScoreRing
title: ScoreRing
wrapsNative: ProgressView(value:total:) with a private ProgressViewStyle that draws the ring and the number
summary: A circular score: a ring filled to the score with the number written in the middle, coloured by the band the score falls in.
whenToUse: For a score out of a fixed maximum that people compare to good and bad bands: profile strength, SEO score, health score.
whenNotToUse: For progress of a task, use ProgressView with the monarchCircular style. For a value on a range without a score, use MonarchGauge.
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, value: Double?, max: Double = 100, description: String? = nil, color: MonarchScoreRingColor = .auto, thresholds: [MonarchScoreRingThreshold] = MonarchScoreRingThreshold.defaults, size: MonarchScoreRingSize = .md, showsMax: Bool? = nil, format: (@Sendable (Double) -> String)? = nil, labels: MonarchScoreRingLabels = MonarchScoreRingLabels())
enum MonarchScoreRingColor { case auto, accent, tone(MonarchTone) }
enum MonarchScoreRingSize { case sm, md, lg }
struct MonarchScoreRingThreshold { init(minimum: Double, tone: MonarchTone); static let defaults: [MonarchScoreRingThreshold] }
struct MonarchScoreRingLabels { var name: String?; var valueText: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)?; var ofMax: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var noValue: String? }

options.name: label
options.description: Shown under the ring and read as its name.

options.name: value
options.description: The score. nil shows an empty ring and a dash. Limited to 0 through max.

options.name: max
options.description: The top of the scale. Zero, negative or infinite values fall back to 100.

options.name: description
options.description: A second line under the label.

options.name: color
options.description: auto takes the tone of the band; accent is the brand colour for a score with no good or bad meaning; tone(_) is fixed.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: The bands auto uses: 80 success, 60 info, 40 warning, below 40 danger.

options.name: size
options.description: sm 48, md 80, lg 120 points before Dynamic Type.

options.name: showsMax
options.description: Shows "/ 100" under the number. By default on md and lg.

options.name: format
options.description: Formats the number in the middle and in the spoken value. By default a whole number in the current locale.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Score", "78 out of 100", "/ 100" and "No score yet".

states.name: no score
states.description: An empty track and a dash in the middle; read as "No score yet".

states.name: zero
states.description: An empty track and the number 0.

appearance: The track is the muted background colour; the arc is the solid colour of the band's tone, the solid accent, or the muted text colour for the neutral tone. The number is the default text colour and "/ 100" and the description are muted.
platformNotes: The web takes the diameter and the stroke width in pixels; here three sizes keep the ring on the spacing scale, and the ring scales with Dynamic Type. The web's accent tone is the accent case of MonarchScoreRingColor, because MonarchTone has no accent case. Android shares the name and the options.
accessibility: The ring and the label are one element, named by the label or "Score", with the value "78 out of 100" or "No score yet".
The score is always written as a number, so the band colour is never the only signal.
The description is separate static text.
The ring scales with Dynamic Type and the number shrinks to stay inside it.
edgeCases: Scores above max are shown as max, below zero as zero; not-a-number counts as no score.
A label longer than the ring wraps and is centred under it.
The arc starts at the top. Its direction in right-to-left layouts follows SwiftUI's handling of the Circle shape and has not been checked on a device.

examples.title: Bands
A rating on a five-point scale in the accent colour
examples.code:
MonarchScoreRing(
    "Rating",
    value: 4.3,
    max: 5,
    color: .accent,
    size: .sm,
    format: { $0.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(1))) }
)
